page.title: sus.bot | robots.txt checker
page.description: Free robots.txt checker. Fetch any site's robots.txt, see which search engines and AI crawlers are allowed or blocked, test paths against the rules, and check how the server responds to different user-agents.
page.h1: Check which crawlers your robots.txt lets in
page.intro: Enter a website. sus.bot fetches its robots.txt and shows which pages each search engine and AI crawler may visit. It also lists the paths the file reveals to anyone who reads it. The check runs in your browser and is free.
page.urlHint: We fetch /robots.txt from the site's origin. Paths and query strings are ignored.
page.agentsIntro: Resolved per crawler with RFC 9309 matching: the most specific group wins, then the longest rule, and ties go to Allow.
page.accessIntro: Request the file again through the proxy with each crawler's real user-agent string. A different status or body means the server treats that crawler differently (bot blocking, WAF rules, cloaking).
page.securityIntro: Disallow rules that point at places attackers look for first. This checks what the file reveals, not whether the paths exist or are protected.
page.reconIntro: What a stranger learns about this site from the file alone: the platform it runs on, cloud buckets, other hostnames, API entry points, data feeds, file types, and notes left in comments. Nothing here is fetched or probed; it is read straight from the text.
page.footerRfc: Rule matching follows RFC 9309 and Google's published crawler behaviour.
page.footerBy: A free tool by Sitefig.
page.noscript: This tool runs entirely in your browser and needs JavaScript.
parser.tooLarge: The file is {kib} KiB. Crawlers only read the first 500 KiB and ignore the rest.
parser.bom: The file starts with a UTF-8 byte-order mark. Most parsers strip it, but saving without one is safer.
parser.notFieldValue: Line is not in "field: value" form and is ignored.
parser.misspelling: "{raw}" is read as "{field}". Google tolerates the misspelling; other crawlers may not.
parser.emptyUserAgent: Empty User-agent value. This group matches no crawler.
parser.invalidToken: "{value}" is not a valid product token. This group matches no crawler.
parser.tokenTail: Only "{token}" is used for matching. The rest of "{value}" is ignored.
parser.ruleBeforeAgent: {directive} appears before any User-agent line and is ignored.
parser.emptyDisallow: Empty Disallow means "allow everything" and has no effect.
parser.pathNoSlash: Path "{value}" does not start with "/" and will never match. Did you mean "/{value}"?
parser.crawlDelayBeforeAgent: Crawl-delay appears before any User-agent line and is ignored.
parser.crawlDelayDuplicate: Duplicate Crawl-delay in this group. The first one is kept.
parser.crawlDelayNonStandard: Crawl-delay is not part of RFC 9309. Bing honours it; Google and Yandex ignore it.
parser.sitemapInvalid: Sitemap value "{value}" is not an absolute http(s) URL.
parser.hostDuplicate: Duplicate Host. The first one is kept.
parser.hostObsolete: Host was a Yandex-only directive for naming the main mirror. Yandex dropped it in 2018; no crawler uses it now. Redirect to the preferred hostname instead.
parser.cleanParamMalformed: Clean-param is malformed. Expected "Clean-param: p1&p2 /path-prefix" with parameter names made of letters, digits, "_", "-" and ".".
parser.cleanParamTooLong: Clean-param is longer than {max} characters, the limit Yandex accepts.
parser.cleanParamInfo: Clean-param is a Yandex-only directive. Yandex ignores the listed query parameters when crawling; other crawlers ignore the directive.
parser.noindex: Noindex in robots.txt is not supported by any major search engine. Use a robots meta tag or X-Robots-Tag header instead.
parser.noRules: No rules found. Every crawler may access everything.
parser.emptyGroup: This group has no rules, so matching crawlers may access everything.
parser.tokenRepeated: "{token}" appears in {n} groups. RFC 9309 merges their rules; some older crawlers only use the first.
parser.starBlocksAll: The "*" group disallows the whole site. Every crawler without its own group is blocked entirely.
parser.noSitemap: No Sitemap line. Optional, but it helps crawlers discover URLs.
seo.trailingSlash.allow: Trailing slash trap: "{path}" is a prefix, so it also allows {path}s, {path}-old and {path}2. Did you mean "{path}/" for the directory, or "{path}$" for only that URL?
seo.trailingSlash.disallow: Trailing slash trap: "{path}" is a prefix, so it also blocks {path}s, {path}-old and {path}2. Did you mean "{path}/" for the directory, or "{path}$" for only that URL?
seo.selfBlock: Self-block: "Disallow: {path}" matches /robots.txt. Google always fetches robots.txt regardless, but other crawlers may honour this and stop reading your rules altogether.
seo.caseSensitive: Case-sensitive: "{path}" only matches URLs with exactly this casing. "{lower}" would not match. Check the site's real URL casing.
seo.redundant: Redundant: "{rule}" never takes effect because "{winner}" on line {line} already covers every path it matches{scope}.
seo.overridden: Overridden: "{rule}" never wins because "{winner}" on line {line} takes precedence on every path it matches{scope}.
sitemap.duplicate: Duplicate Sitemap: this URL is already listed on line {line}.
sitemap.protocolMismatch: Protocol mismatch: the site is served over https but this sitemap is listed as http. Crawlers will hit a redirect on every fetch, or an insecure copy. Use {url}.
sitemap.httpsOnHttp: The sitemap is https but the site was reached over http. Fine if the site redirects to https; otherwise list the sitemap with the protocol the site actually uses.
sitemap.crossDomain: Cross-domain sitemap: hosted on {host}, not {site}. Google only accepts it if both sites are verified by the same owner in Search Console (cross-site submission). Other search engines may ignore it.
sitemap.otherSubdomain: The sitemap is on a different host of the same domain ({host}). Listing it here is what allows it to contain {site} URLs, so this is fine.
lint.absoluteUrl: "{rule}" is an absolute URL. Rules must be paths, so this never matches anything. It also publishes the hostname.
lint.absoluteUrl.hint: "{rule}" is an absolute URL. Rules must be paths, so this never matches anything. Did you mean "{path}"? It also publishes the hostname.
fetch.warn.redirectLimit: More than five redirects. RFC 9309 lets crawlers give up at that point, and Google then treats the file as a 404: no restrictions.
fetch.warn.redirectSameSite: robots.txt redirected to {host}. A www/non-www or https redirect like this is fine; crawlers follow it.
fetch.warn.redirectOtherHost: robots.txt redirected to a different host, {to}. Crawlers apply the file they land on as this site's robots.txt, so {from} is governed by {to}'s rules.
fetch.warn.notRobotsPath: The redirect ended at {path}, not /robots.txt. Crawlers still parse whatever they received as robots.txt.
fetch.error.unsupportedProtocol: Only http and https URLs are supported.
fetch.error.notHostname: "{host}" does not look like a hostname.
fetch.error.cors: Direct fetch was blocked. The site does not send CORS headers for robots.txt.
fetch.error.noProxy: The proxy is not configured. Set WORKER_URL in js/config.js.
fetch.error.proxyTimeout: The proxy did not answer in time.
fetch.error.proxyUnreadable: The proxy returned an unreadable response (HTTP {status}).
fetch.error.rateLimited: Too many requests: the proxy is rate-limited right now. Wait a minute and try again.
fetch.error.paused: The proxy is switched off at the moment, so only sites that send CORS headers can be fetched. Paste the robots.txt instead.
fetch.error.originRefused: The proxy refused this page's origin. Add it to ALLOWED_ORIGINS in worker/wrangler.toml.
fetch.error.noProxyFallback: {reason} No proxy is configured, so the file cannot be read. Paste its contents instead.
security.reconWarning: Security note: Disallow lines are publicly visible and often scanned by attackers for reconnaissance. robots.txt is not access control. Anything listed here should be protected by authentication, removed from the web root, or marked noindex with an HTTP header instead.
security.category.admin.label: Admin / internal
security.category.admin.advice: Protect with authentication and send an X-Robots-Tag: noindex header. Listing it here only advertises where the login is.
security.category.staging.label: Staging / dev
security.category.staging.advice: Take staging and test environments off the public internet, or restrict them by IP or login. Use a noindex header rather than robots.txt.
security.category.backups.label: Backups & archives
security.category.backups.advice: Backups and archives should not be reachable over HTTP at all. Move them outside the web root and verify the URL returns 404.
security.category.secrets.label: Secrets & config
security.category.secrets.advice: Configuration files, version-control folders and credentials must never be web-accessible. Block them at the server and check they return 403 or 404.
security.category.api.label: Private APIs & debug
security.category.api.advice: Internal APIs and debug endpoints need authentication or a network allowlist. Crawlers are not the threat here; scripted scanners are.
security.category.data.label: User data & uploads
security.category.data.advice: Turn off directory listing and make sure private files require a login. A Disallow only asks polite crawlers to look away.
security.reason.versioned: Versioned path, often an old or unreleased version
security.reason.configFile: Configuration, version control or credential file

recon.cloud.risk.storage: Bucket and account names can be probed for public listing, read or write permissions.
recon.cloud.risk.cdn: Reveals the CDN vendor and distribution or account identifier.
recon.cloud.risk.hosting: Reveals the hosting provider and project name, often for a non-production copy.
recon.cloud.risk.platform: Confirms the site platform and its asset store.

recon.api.note.docs: Interactive docs and OpenAPI files list every endpoint and parameter.

md.actions.redirectChain: Fix the redirect chain on /robots.txt: crawlers give up after five hops and treat the file as missing.

md.actions.trailingSlash: Decide whether {rules} should end in "/" (directory) or "$" (exact URL); as written they also match longer paths{where}.

md.actions.noSlash: Add the leading "/" to {paths} that can never match{where}.

md.actions.crawlDelay: Treat Crawl-delay as Bing-only; use Search Console crawl settings for Google.
md.actions.starBlocked: Confirm that blocking the whole site for every crawler without its own group is intended.

md.actions.envHosts: Remove non-production hostnames from the file and put those environments behind authentication: {list}.
md.actions.personal: Strip names, email addresses, IPs and ticket IDs from comments; the file is public.
md.actions.bom: Save the file as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark.
md.actions.none: No action needed. The file is clean.

ui.summary.html.title: The server returned HTML

ui.summary.noStar.title: No "*" group

parser.utf16: The file is UTF-16 encoded. RFC 9309 requires UTF-8, and many crawlers will not find a single valid line. Save it as UTF-8.
parser.htmlFragment: HTML markup ("{tag}") found in robots.txt. It usually comes from a theme, plugin or cache layer. Those lines are invalid and can break the directive next to them.
parser.pluginOutput: A caching or minification plugin has appended its output to robots.txt. Exclude /robots.txt from that plugin.
parser.serverErrorOutput: robots.txt contains a server error message, such as a PHP warning or a stack trace. It can reveal file paths on the server and it breaks the lines around it.
parser.invalidUtf8: The file is not valid UTF-8. RFC 9309 requires UTF-8; the characters that could not be decoded are lost.
parser.longLine: Line is {chars} characters long. A line that long is generated, not written, and some crawlers truncate it.
parser.gluedComment: "{directive}" is part of a comment because a line break is missing before it, so crawlers ignore this rule.
lint.commentedRule: This line is a commented-out "{directive}" rule and has no effect.
parser.invisibleChar: An invisible character sits in front of a directive name. Crawlers read the name as unknown and skip the line. Retype the line.
parser.homoglyph: "{field}" is written with a letter from another alphabet that looks the same. Crawlers do not recognise the directive. Retype it in plain Latin letters.
parser.fullwidthColon: A full-width colon is used instead of ":". Crawlers only accept the plain colon.
parser.junkBeforeField: "{junk}" sits before "{field}". Crawlers read the whole name, so the directive is ignored. Remove what comes before it.
parser.hashInValue: "{value}" is cut at "#", because "#" starts a comment. The rule applies to "{truncated}". Remove the fragment; URL fragments are never sent to the server.
parser.crawlDelayHigh: Crawl-delay of {seconds} seconds allows about {pages} pages a day. Bing honours this; large sites will not be crawled fully.
parser.wildcardOnly: "Disallow: {value}" is not RFC 9309. Google reads it as "block everything", other crawlers read it as a literal path. Write "Disallow: /" if you mean the whole site.
parser.spaceInPath: "{value}" contains a space. URLs never contain raw spaces; use %20 or split the rule.
parser.regexSyntax: "{value}" uses regular-expression syntax. robots.txt only supports "*" and "$", so the other characters match literally.
parser.nonAsciiPath: "{value}" contains non-ASCII characters. RFC 9309 matches percent-encoded paths; most crawlers encode it for you, some do not.
parser.bareUrl: This line is only a URL and is ignored. If this is your sitemap, write "Sitemap: {url}".
parser.metaRobots: "{field}" is a meta-robots value, not a robots.txt directive. Use a meta robots tag or the X-Robots-Tag header instead.
parser.aiDirective: "{field}" is a proposed AI-policy extension, not part of RFC 9309. Crawlers that follow the standard ignore it. Use User-agent groups for the AI crawlers you want to block.
parser.nonStandardDirective: "{field}" is not part of RFC 9309. A few crawlers once honoured it; today it is ignored.
parser.contentSignal: Content-Signal states how this site may be used ({value}). It is Cloudflare's extension, not part of RFC 9309, and only the crawlers that support it will follow it.
parser.contentSignalInvalid: Content-Signal is malformed at {parts}. Each entry is search, ai-input or ai-train, set to yes or no.
parser.notFieldValue.hint: Line has no ":" between a directive and its value. Did you mean "{field}"?
security.injectedCode: robots.txt contains script, iframe or hidden-link markup. That is a common sign that the site or a plugin has been compromised for SEO spam. Check the server for malicious code.
seo.queryStringBlock: "Disallow: {path}" blocks every URL with a query string for all crawlers, including paginated, filtered and tracked landing pages.
seo.assetBlock: "Disallow: {path}" blocks scripts or styles. Search engines need them to render the page.
seo.cssJsBlock: "Disallow: {path}" blocks CSS or JavaScript files. Search engines render the page before they judge it, and a page without its assets looks broken to them.
seo.imageBlock: "Disallow: {path}" keeps images out of image search for all crawlers.
lint.legacyBadBots: This file blocks {n} old scrapers and e-mail harvesters that never obeyed robots.txt. The list has no effect; block them at the server if you need to.
fetch.warn.serverError: robots.txt answered {status}. Google treats a server error as "block everything" and stops crawling the site while it lasts.
fetch.warn.rateLimited: robots.txt answered 429 Too Many Requests. Google treats that like a server error and stops crawling the site while it lasts.
fetch.warn.forbidden: robots.txt answered {status}. Crawlers treat that as "no restrictions" and crawl everything.
fetch.warn.contentType: robots.txt is served as {type}. Serve it as text/plain; some crawlers ignore other types.
fetch.warn.contentTypeMissing: robots.txt is served without a Content-Type header. Serve it as text/plain.
fetch.warn.htmlBody: An HTML page is served at /robots.txt with status 200. Crawlers find no rules, and a missing robots.txt is treated as "crawl everything".
security.category.version.label: Version disclosure
security.category.version.advice: These files name the software and its version, which is the first thing an attacker looks for. Delete them from the server instead of hiding them here.
security.category.maintenance.label: Maintenance scripts
security.category.maintenance.advice: Installers and update scripts must not be reachable after setup. Remove them, or restrict them by IP address.
security.category.server.label: Server internals
security.category.server.advice: These paths belong to the server, not the site. If nothing runs there, remove the rule; it only points at them.
security.reason.versionFile: File that names the software version
security.reason.licenseFile: Licence file that identifies the software
security.reason.xmlrpc: XML-RPC endpoint, a common brute-force target
security.reason.dependencies: Dependency directory that reveals the libraries in use
security.reason.platformDefault: Default path of {platform}, published by every site on it
recon.generators.note: The file was generated. Change it where the tool is configured, not by hand, or the next save overwrites it.
md.recon.generators: Written by {list}. Change the file where that tool is configured; editing it by hand is overwritten on the next save.
